findings.obs_text: In Gen 26:9 Abimelech calls Isaac and Isaac gives the thought behind his lie, and in 2Ki 5:11 Naaman thought the prophet would call on the Lord: call is the act the thought expected. In Jer 3:19 the Lord thought Israel would call him Father, and in Jon 1:6 the captain urges Jonah to call on his god in the hope the god will give a thought to them. In Isa 7:14, Mat 1:23 and Luk 1:31 call is naming the child, with conceive in its bodily sense.
findings.grounds: And I thought you would call me, My Father

older.finding: Call is a purposeful act of the inner being turned to God: calling or crying out to the Lord, or on his name, in need, trust, praise or worship, or refusing to.
older.reason: it states a face or use of the call words; the call collection owns it

older.finding: Call is here the outward use of the Lord's name over others (a formula spoken over a person or thing); it is the outward act and bears on them, with no inner operation of the speaker named.
older.reason: it states a face or use of the call words; the call collection owns it

older.finding: Call here only names, designates or labels a person, place or thing (to be called such a name, to call it so); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.
older.reason: it states a face or use of the call words; the call collection owns it

older.finding: Call, in a naming, voices the inner state of the one who names, stated in the verse (grief, hope, thanks, trust or confession): the name is a purposeful act of the heart made audible.
older.reason: it states a face or use of the call words; the call collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Deu 15:9 the people are to take care lest an unworthy thought be in the heart: the thought is what is to be guarded against. In Luk 8:18 take care is how to hear, and what one thinks he has may be taken. In Mat 22:16 care and opinion name Jesus not regarding a person's standing.
findings.grounds: Take care lest there be an unworthy thought in your heart

findings.obs_text: In Dan 5:6, Dan 5:10 and Dan 7:28 the thoughts alarm and the color changes: the change of face goes with the alarming thoughts, and in Dan 5:10 the queen bids the king's color not change. In Dan 7:25 the one against the Most High thinks to change the times and the law: there the change is what the thought intends.

older.finding: 11.2 New heart, new spirit — renewal of the inner seat (M45): "my color changed, but I kept the matter in my heart" (Dan 7:28); [Claude reading] Renewal is predicated of heart and spirit together (Eze 11:19; 18:31; 36:26; Psa 51:10). Eze 18:31 makes it the person's task and Eze 36:26 makes it God's gift. Batch C §8.3 already noted the heart / spirit / flesh triad in these verses.
older.reason: it states how change works in a person; the change collection owns it

older.finding: What carries it instead of a seat: the question spoken aloud: "What does this mean?" (Act 2:12); "who is this about whom I hear such things?" (Luk 9:9, context); the gaze: "The disciples looked at one another" (Joh 13:22); a reflexive pronoun: Act 10:17 "inwardly perplexed" is *en heautō*, "in himself". findings.obs_text: In Psa 50:21 the people thought God was like themselves because he was silent, and he now rebukes them: the false thought about God is met by his rebuke.
findings.grounds: you thought that I was one like yourself

findings.obs_text: In Pro 15:26 the thoughts of the wicked stand against gracious words that are pure. In Phili 4:8 whatever is pure is among what the believers are to think on: the thinking is directed to purity.
findings.grounds: whatever is pure, whatever is lovely
